# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display `0`, blue indicator light, and three wires in order: green, yellow, red. I cannot know what the manual instructs or what the blind monkey’s thumbs-up gesture means, so I am relaying the visual facts plainly to both teammates.

```text
speak(text="I see display 0. The light is blue. Wires 1, 2, 3 are green, yellow, red respectively.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains unchanged: display `0`, blue light, and wires green/yellow/red. I saw Mute’s thumbs-up, but its meaning has not been established; I should ask Mute to interpret the manual for this exact configuration so Blind can act safely.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb is still display 0 with a blue light and wires green, yellow, red. Please state the manual instruction for this configuration, including what Blind must do.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb still shows the same unchanged state. Mute’s repeated thumbs-up only confirms receipt or agreement; it conveys no established instruction to me. Since Blind can hear but cannot see, I will tell Blind not to act yet and ask Mute to speak the manual’s exact procedure directly to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. I have only visual details: display 0, blue light, wires green, yellow, red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction directly to Blind now; gestures do not tell me the procedure.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute has sent a different gesture, 🤟, but I cannot infer its meaning from an unestablished signal. I will again provide Blind the visible configuration and direct Mute to communicate the manual’s exact instruction by speech, which Blind can hear.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="No visible change: display 0, blue light, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Do not act on gestures whose meaning is unknown.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret gestures without an agreed code. Speak the exact manual instruction to Blind.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The visible bomb state remains unchanged, and I have received no interpretable new information. Mute has the manual and can speak to Blind, who is the only one able to operate the bomb. I will not guess what the gestures mean or instruct Blind to take an unsafe action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give Blind the exact manual instruction by voice, based on display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged, and there are still no new signals to interpret. I have already transmitted the complete visible state; the safe next step depends on Mute communicating the manual’s instruction to Blind. I will avoid inventing a code or recommending an action.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains at display `0` with a blue light and wires green, yellow, red. No new information has reached me. Since Mute has the manual and Blind can hear and act, I will give Mute a final direct prompt to communicate the exact required operation, while reminding Blind of the visible configuration.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do for display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Blind must hear the complete operation before acting.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state is unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Wait for Mute's exact manual instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged, and I have no new information from the manual. I cannot hear whether Mute has spoken to Blind, so I will establish a simple visible confirmation channel with Blind: after hearing this request, Blind should gesture thumbs-up if Mute gave a complete instruction, or thumbs-down otherwise. I will also prompt Mute to speak the instruction directly.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="After Mute speaks, signal me with thumbs-up if you received a complete manual instruction, or thumbs-down if you did not.")
speak(to="mute", text="Speak the complete manual instruction to Blind now. Blind will confirm receipt with thumbs-up or thumbs-down.")
```
